html:
SMTO-ART-0024 — SMTO blocked a file request that came from another site

GUID: 28bc486f-4081-4cac-ab1a-15cc8acf54db
Slug: artifact-cross-site-denied
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO refused to open or change a Task's files because the request came from another website, app, or a different address for SMTO. No files were opened, changed, or deleted.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open SMTO by typing its usual address or using your bookmark, instead of following a file link from an email, a chat app, or another website. SMTO only hands out Task files to requests that start on its own pages, so links from elsewhere are blocked.
  2. Open the conversation, find the Run that made the file, and select Artifacts from this run to view or download it. Files opened from this list are requested by SMTO's own page, so the request is accepted.
  3. If you were changing Artifact retention for this conversation or selecting Retry collection, open SMTO at the address you were given, then check the list before doing it again. These changes are refused when the page was loaded from a different address, and checking first shows whether the change already took effect.

What success looks like

  • The file opens or downloads from Artifacts from this run, and a retention change shows Saved. under the setting.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the address shown in your browser, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't use browser add-ons or turn off security settings to get around this block; it protects your files from other websites.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The artifact API rejected the request because the browser marked it Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, or its Origin header did not match the Server's own base URL.

What this means

  • Artifact access/settings/reconcile checks reject a cross-site fetch or an Origin different from the owning application origin. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact access/settings/reconcile checks reject a cross-site fetch or an Origin different from the owning application origin.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the intended application origin and supported session/API route without weakening origin checks.

How to fix it

  • ArtifactAccess.require rejects any artifact request with Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site, and the artifact-session, artifact-retention (PUT) and artifacts/reconcile routes also reject an Origin that differs from request.base_url. Use the in-app artifact controls on SMTO's own origin; if SMTO is behind a reverse proxy, forward the original Host and scheme so base_url matches the public origin, and keep the origin checks enabled.
  • Use the artifact controls on the owning SMTO origin with the supported session or API credential. Keep origin checks enabled.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The action originates from the authenticated owning application flow.

What not to do

  • Do not silently substitute a different target for a saved run or move its existing execution authority.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
